question: Should I put my college grade point average on my resume?

retrieved.label: S1
retrieved.text:
●​ No resume alone is going to get you a job. A successful job hunt is equal parts of five
     things–exploration, research, positioning, networking, and job hunt
         ○​ You have to explore the industry/role you specifically want, research the
            company you want, position yourself accordingly, network to get an inside
            referral, and then submit your resume.
                ■​ Recruiters love referrals because data shows that referred candidates get
                    hired faster and stay longer
  ●​ The average recruiter is juggling 30-40 open roles and the average job listing attracts
     250 resumes. The best recruiters used Linkedin, and they search by job title

retrieved.label: S2
retrieved.location: vault/raw/Aug 2025 - Resume Only Workshop.pdf p.2 §Resume Workshop #2 (lines 1-12)
retrieved.text:
○​ ATS systems neither accept nor reject your resume; it indexes them to make it
               easier for the recruiter to read your resume. Haas’ standard format makes this
               easier by design
         ○​ Recruiters don’t put any value in algorithm-generated resume “rating.” They rely
               on 8-second personal, “human” scan
 ●​   Put all “applied innovation” classwork in your experience because it is work with clients
 ●​   Remove undergrad GPA because the moment it’s added it opens you up to comparison
 ●​   Remove undergrad awards unless you have space
 ●​   Make sure you have an additional section and be humorous to entice the reader to ask
      you about it. The section should be 1-3 lines
         ○​ Example: Interests: Amateur backyard farmer, optimistic AI futurist, and
               washed-up distance runner (former D1 athlete.)

retrieved.label: S3
retrieved.location: vault/raw/Aug 2025 - Resume Only Workshop.pdf p.2 §Resume Workshop #1 (lines 33-37)
retrieved.text:
●​ Gen AI quality controls–is everything true, check for too much jargon (including
    adjectives and adverbs), 3-letter acronyms, read it outloud, and ensure the bullets
    include the three elements (what, how, why)
 ●​ If you don’t know what the impact for a bullet is (this happens often in consulting), put
    down what the projected impact would be

retrieved.label: S4
retrieved.text:
○​ Example outreach message “I came across your profile and, as a fellow [College]
            grad. I’d be thrilled to learn about your experience with [Role.] Any chance you
            have 10 minutes to chat next week? I'd love to get your advice!
  ●​ Networking question ideas
        ○​ It's great to connect with you via [Name] - thanks for making the time!

retrieved.label: S5
retrieved.location: vault/raw/Aug 2025 - Resume & Networking Training.pdf p.3 §Session #1 - Resume Bullets (lines 1-20)
retrieved.text:
○​ How: What skills you used to make that work object (skills should be tailored to
              the employer/role)
          ○​ Impact: Measurable outcome ideally
          ○​ Why: Why was it important, was it part of a company’s bigger strategy? How
              often did you do it, etc.
●​   Start with “impact” if it is large; start with “how” if you are pivoting industry, or potentially
     role, where the vocabulary is not the same
●​   All bullets should be explicit rather than intentionally mysterious to generate curiosity or a
     follow-up question
●​   Adjectives and adverbs is what makes a bullet long
●​   Use abbreviations only if you are moving within the same industry or function
●​   Gen AI use cases
          ○​ Rewrite your bullets
          ○​ Point out what’s moving
          ○​ Improve readability
●​   Gen AI quality controls–is everything true, check for too much jargon (including
adjectives and adverbs), 3-letter acronyms, read it outloud, and ensure the bullets
     include the three elements (what, how, why)
●​   If you don’t know what the impact for a bullet is (this happens often in consulting), put
     down what the projected impact would be

answer: Remove your undergraduate GPA from your resume because adding it opens you up to comparison [S2].
